fallback.greeting: Thank you for making time, Mr. President. There is something we can move forward today, if you're willing to put your support behind it.
fallback.trusted: We've earned some trust together. I'd like to use it to get something lasting done.
fallback.strained: I'll be direct. People are watching what we deliver, and the next promise needs to mean something.
fallback.pending: Before we start anything new, let's talk about the commitment you already made. The deadline is getting closer.
fallback.met: My recommendation is on your desk. I'll get back to work while you consider the policy.
fallback.busy: Your appointments are full for this quarter. We can review the file now and talk next quarter.
fallback.closed: The decision has been filed. Let's see how the quarter turns out and pick this up at our next meeting.
fallback.ended: The term is over. Whatever happens next, the record will show the choices we made here.
fallback.resigned: This office is no longer represented by this adviser. An acting replacement must be appointed before meetings can resume.
fallback.promise: Then we have your word. I'll tell the team to expect movement. Please make sure the policy reaches the target before our deadline.
fallback.compromise: It's a smaller commitment, but it gives us something to work with. I'll hold you to that timetable.
fallback.listen: I appreciate being heard. I'll keep making the case, but I won't tell anyone we have a commitment yet.
fallback.reassure: I'll take you at your word. The original deadline still stands.
fallback.extend: One more quarter. That is the room we have, so let's use it.
fallback.withdraw: Understood. I'll explain that the commitment has been withdrawn. That will not be an easy conversation.
fallback.refused: We can't record that action right now. Let's check the appointment schedule and the terms of the commitment.

chen.greeting: Mr. President, the people I meet don't talk in budget categories. They talk about the rent, the commute, and whether their children will have a better start. I brought one concrete request.
chen.trusted: We've shown people that this administration can deliver. Now let's give them a reason to believe the progress will last.
chen.strained: I need something I can take back to the families waiting on us. Another announcement won't be enough. Can we agree on a policy and a date?
chen.pending: I still have your commitment on my calendar. The team is ready; they need the policy to catch up with the promise.
chen.promise: Thank you. I'll put the target and the deadline in writing. If we deliver, this becomes more than a good meeting in a beautiful room.
chen.compromise: I can work with a smaller first step. Just make it a real one. People can tell the difference between a start and a delay.
chen.listen: Then let me leave the file with you. Behind each number is someone waiting for an answer.
chen.withdraw: I'll tell the people who were counting on it. But rebuilding their trust will take more than another promise.

ruiz.greeting: Good to see you, Mr. President. Back home, they don't ask which office is responsible. They ask why nothing has changed yet. Help me give them a better answer.
ruiz.trusted: My communities are beginning to see the results. Keep showing up for them and they'll keep showing up for you.
ruiz.strained: I spent political capital defending this administration. I need to know you're prepared to spend some of yours for the people I represent.
ruiz.pending: I told my people we had an agreement. Before I get on the next flight home, tell me we're still on track.
ruiz.promise: That's something I can take home. I'll stand beside you on it. Now give me a result we can both defend.
ruiz.compromise: Not everything I wanted, but a governor learns to recognize an opening. Let's get this first step done.
ruiz.listen: All right. I came to make the case, and you've heard it. Just remember that waiting is a decision for the people living with it.
ruiz.extend: I can buy us one more quarter. After that, I won't be able to explain the delay away.

brooks.greeting: Mr. President, every choice here has a price. My job is to make sure we understand it before we make the announcement. Let's look at one decision we can afford to take seriously.
brooks.trusted: The numbers are moving, and credibility is an asset too. Let's protect both while we decide where to spend next.
brooks.strained: I can defend a difficult trade-off. I cannot defend a promise made without a plan to fund it. Let's be precise this time.
brooks.pending: I've kept the original target in the forecast. If we're changing course, I need to know before we run out of time.
brooks.promise: I'll record the commitment. Remember: changing a setting is the start. Implementation takes time, and the budget still has to balance around it.
brooks.compromise: A narrower commitment with a longer runway. That is manageable. I'll revise the assumptions accordingly.
brooks.listen: Fair enough. There is value in looking at the trade-offs before signing anything. The figures are in the policy file.
brooks.reassure: Then the forecast stays as it is. Reassurance buys goodwill, not extra time.

bell.greeting: Mr. President, a good idea still needs people willing to vote for it. Give me something concrete, and I'll tell you what I can sell to the coalition.
bell.trusted: You've kept enough of your word that people are taking my calls. Let's turn that goodwill into something we can pass.
bell.strained: I'm hearing a lot of doubt on the Hill. If I ask members to take a risk for you, I need to know you'll hold up your end.
bell.pending: The coalition remembers the deal. Before I go back to them, let's make sure we're delivering the part we control.
bell.promise: Good. I'll put my name behind that. And if the policy needs an act of Congress to reach full strength, bring it to the floor. A promise is not a vote.
bell.compromise: I can describe that as a first step. But nobody should mistake a compromise for the finish line.
bell.listen: Then I won't count it as a commitment. When you're ready to move, bring me a position I can take into the room.
bell.withdraw: I'll make the calls. Some people will understand; others will remember this the next time we need their votes.
